3. Forensic Quality-of-Earnings & True Free Cash Flow Bridge (Q4 FY26)

Non-Cash BTC Mark-to-Market vs. Core Mining Loss +$305.57M Mark Gain

CleanSpark's +$0.04 GAAP EPS ($9.80M Net Income) and $345.36M Adjusted EBITDA were driven by a +$305.57M non-cash ASC 350-60 Bitcoin fair-value gain and +$40.22M collateral gain, masking a -$114.61M core ex-mark operating loss and $171.67M in non-cash impairment on Sandersville legacy mining gear.

Sandersville AI/HPC CapEx Surge ($237.64M) & Restricted Debt Escrow $2.14B Ring-Fenced Cash

Standalone Q4 FY26 PP&E/CIP CapEx jumped to $237.64M (FY26 total $318.26M minus 9M $80.62M; Data Center Infrastructure CIP reached $351.85M per 10-K Note 17), funded via the $2.276B 7.875% senior secured project notes due 2031. Excluding $2,143.35M of restricted cash, parent unrestricted liquidity stands at $204.76M cash + $1,130.50M BTC (13,530 BTC).

Digital Asset Management & Miner CapEx Freeze $30.6M Derivative Proceeds

Operating Cash Flow improved sequentially from -$112.33M in Q3 to -$59.10M in Q4 FY26, aided by $30.6M in FY26 derivative proceeds and $609.21M full-year BTC monetization proceeds. Management trimmed active miners by 17% to ~200,000 units (14.8 J/Th) and halted material ASIC refresh CapEx ($9.97M Q4 miner payments).

4. What Management Did Right vs. Wrong & Earnings Call Q&A Forensic Audit

Execution Wins (What Management Did Right)

Non-Recourse $2.276B Sandersville Financing & Cost Lock De-Risked Buildout

Issued $2.276B of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031, capping parent equity outlay under $100M, achieving 100% basis-of-design alignment, locking a turnkey lump-sum EPCM contract, and securing all permits on schedule for Nov 2027 RFS.

Texas 585 MW Batch Zero Baseload + 300 MW Studied Load Grid Scarcity Moat

Secured Conditional Batch Zero Baseload status across Sealy (285 MW) and Brazoria Phase 1 (300 MW), TCEQ permits, and Batch Zero Studied Load for Brazoria Phase 2 (300 MW)—plus Washington, GA study up to 500 MW.

Mining CapEx Discipline & 14.8 J/Th Efficiency Gain Capital Stewardship

Trimmed 17% of legacy miners (~200k active), improved fleet efficiency 11.4% YoY to 14.8 J/Th, halted material ASIC CapEx, and preserved $1.34B liquidity ($204.8M cash + 13,530 BTC) with zero Q4 common equity dilution.

Execution Drags & Risks (What Went Wrong / Open Risks)

Texas Tenant Exclusivity Expiration (Sealy & Brazoria) Near-Term Overhang

Disclosed that tenant exclusivity at Sealy and Brazoria expired amid temporary ERCOT regulatory uncertainty, pushing definitive Phase-2 AI lease signing past December ERCOT/PUCT meetings.

Top-Line Revenue Miss (-5.33%) & 2.56% Mining Gross Margin Core Margin Squeeze

Revenue fell 45.9% YoY to $120.94M (missing $127.75M consensus) while gross profit ex-D&A compressed to $3.10M (2.56% margin), resulting in -$114.61M core operating loss before non-cash BTC marks.

Elevated Consolidated Debt ($4.08B) & 12-Month Rent Gap Bridge Risk

Total balance sheet debt jumped from $821M to $4,081.10M ($92.2M current + $3,988.9M long-term) following the project notes, while Sandersville triple-net rent does not begin until Nov 2027 (FY28).

Earnings Call Analyst Questions & Forensic Q&A Highlights

Q&A #1: Texas 885 MW Exclusivity Expiration & ERCOT / PUCT Regulatory Catalysts Sell-Side Infrastructure Coverage (Q4 FY26 Call Q&A)

Analyst Question: "With the exclusivity period for the Sealy (285 MW) and Brazoria (up to 600 MW) assets expiring, how should investors interpret the demand backdrop from the Sandersville tenant versus other hyperscalers, and what unlocks binding leases?"

Management Response & Forensic Takeaway: CEO Matt Schultz explained that CleanSpark deliberately avoided locking into rigid lease terms while ERCOT and PUCT interconnection rules were in flux, noting that the market value of energized baseload megawatts has actually appreciated. Management highlighted upcoming December meetings with ERCOT and PUCT as pivotal regulatory milestones and confirmed active commercialization talks continue with both the Sandersville tenant and multiple other investment-grade counterparties.

Q&A #2: Sandersville $2.276B Project Notes Structure, Parent Equity Exposure & Cost Overrun Protection Credit & Institutional Research (Q4 FY26 Call Q&A)

Analyst Question: "Following the $2.276B senior secured notes issuance, how much parent-level equity remains required to reach November 2027 delivery, and how are construction cost overruns mitigated?"

Management Response & Forensic Takeaway: CFO Gary Vecchiarelli confirmed the Sandersville project is 100% funded through the 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031, keeping parent equity contribution under $100M. Management mitigated overrun risk by achieving 100% basis-of-design alignment, signing a turnkey lump-sum EPCM construction contract, pre-paying long-lead electrical equipment, and securing all material zoning and building permits.

Q&A #3: Mining Fleet CapEx Discipline, 17% Unit Reduction & Parent Cash Bridge Through FY27 Digital Infrastructure & Mining Coverage (Q4 FY26 Call Q&A)

Analyst Question: "With mining gross margins compressed and OCF negative before BTC sales, how will CleanSpark manage its ~200,000 ASIC fleet and $1.3B liquidity without diluting common shareholders ahead of late-2027 lease cash flows?"

Management Response & Forensic Takeaway: CFO Gary Vecchiarelli and CBO Harry Sudock emphasized that CleanSpark trimmed 17% of older machines to reach 14.8 J/Th efficiency and will not allocate material CapEx to refresh the Bitcoin mining fleet. Instead, the company will run profitable hashrate and utilize its $204.8M cash, $1.13B Bitcoin treasury (including $30.6M FY26 derivative proceeds), and $310M undrawn credit lines to bridge parent operations until Sandersville pods come online.
